Filling an empty node1->output edge with a 3x3 conv adds capacity and a new path, beating replacement of pool, skip or 1x1.
When edge 0 is none, node 1 is dead, so a conv there revives edges 2 and 4 and yields a larger improvement.
Adding a conv where there was no input->node2 edge adds a parallel path, worth more than replacing pool or skip.
If edge 4 is none, node 1 feeds the output only through edge 2, so removing edge 0 costs less than when node 1 connects directly to the output.
With edge 2 absent, removing edge 1 leaves node 2 with no input and kills the edge-5 path, so the loss is much larger.
When edge 5 is none, edge 4 is the only conv path to the output, so removing it collapses the cell to a near-identity and hurts much more.
If edge 4 is none, removing the edge-3 skip can leave the output with few or no live inputs, which is far more damaging.
Without the input->output skip, a skip on edge 4 adds a near-residual shortcut that helps gradient flow, so it is worth more than when edge 3 already provides one.
